opener: Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
A mirror is a surface that reflects light back to the observer, allowing us to see our own image.
Since the light bounces off the polished side, the image appears clear and in reverse.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
The key difference lies in how each surface handles light: a mirror reflects most of the light, while a piece of paper absorbs and scatters it.
When light is reflected, the angles are preserved, so we get a crisp image.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Sure! A mirror is designed to reflect light, while a window allows light to pass through, so you see the outside world rather than your own reflection.
That’s why a window appears transparent, not reflective.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Interesting thought! If you wrapped a piece of paper in a shiny metal foil, would it reflect light as clearly as a mirror?
The foil would reflect light, but the paper’s texture would still scatter it, making the image fuzzy.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Reflection is the change in direction of a light ray when it bounces off a surface.
The law of reflection states that the incident angle equals the reflected angle.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Think about the surface roughness: a mirror has an extremely smooth polished layer, whereas paper has a rough, fibrous structure.
That roughness scatters the light in many directions, so you don’t get a coherent image.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Not exactly—mirrors reflect most but not all light; some is absorbed or transmitted.
The higher the reflectivity, the clearer the image.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Bouncing back is part of it, but the key is that the surface keeps the light’s angle and intensity.
If the surface changes the angle or spreads the light, the image becomes blurry.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
The color we see from a mirror comes from the light it reflects, not from its own color.
A silvered glass reflects all colors equally, so it appears neutral.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Because paper’s fibers scatter the incoming light in many directions rather than sending it back in a single direction.
The scattered light makes it hard for your eyes to reconstruct a clear image.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Polished metal can act like a mirror if it’s smooth enough, but any imperfections will reduce its reflectivity.
That’s why a freshly polished spoon can sometimes reflect a faint image.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Shiny surfaces do reflect light, but the clarity of the reflection also depends on how the surface is prepared.
A rough shiny surface will still scatter light and give a blurry image.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
It states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, measured from the normal.
This symmetry is what keeps the image upright in a plane mirror.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Because the light that reaches your eyes has been reflected, swapping the left and right sides.
The top and bottom remain the same, so the image is only laterally inverted.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
If you coat paper with a reflective layer, it can reflect light, but the paper’s texture will still scatter it.

Why does a mirror show a clear reflection but a piece of paper doesn't?
Think of a mirror as a polished surface that keeps the light’s path straight, like a perfectly straight hallway.
If the hallway had bumps, the light would scatter, and you wouldn’t see a clear path.
